A1.justification: Both PDFs describe RefinedFields and contain 19 readable pages, including Appendices A–D. The text, equations, tables and figures support a complete comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original RefinedFields experiments, ablations and renderings on Phototourism and NeRF synthetic scenes, including Tables 2 and 5.

after.justification: v3 retains the work's original benchmark results, ablations and qualitative renderings in the main text and appendices.

M1.justification: The alternating K-Planes fitting and Stable Diffusion refinement procedure, LoRA adaptation, architecture and training losses remain unchanged. Algorithm 1 is identical.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same eight NeRF synthetic scenes and three Phototourism landmarks. The Lego experiment using half the training images is also retained.

E2.justification: Table 2 removes Ha-NeRF and CR-NeRF across all three Phototourism scenes, substantially narrowing the principal quality comparison and removing the concurrent state-of-the-art comparator. Both methods remain in Table 3's timing comparison; the other comparator sets are unchanged.

E3.justification: Table 6 revises N1 from 'Epochs K-Planes: 1' to 'Fitting iterations: 30000' and relabels N2=3000 as refining iterations. This changes the reported training budget specification, without establishing that experiments were rerun or implying a 30000-fold increase.

E4.justification: The noFinetuning, noPrior and K-Planes-SS ablations, Lego example and Appendix C feature-plane inspection are retained with the same evidence. No new robustness or sensitivity analysis appears.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests. The reporting of point estimates and averages across synthetic scenes is unchanged.

E6.justification: Changes are confined to removing Ha-NeRF and CR-NeRF quality scores and their associated numerical comparison passages. All retained scores, timing values and visual results are unchanged, including RefinedFields' Phototourism PSNR values of 26.64, 22.26 and 23.42.

T1.justification: Equation 5 replaces an unqualified norm with explicit squared L2 notation, consistent with the refinement loss already specified in Equation 9. This clarifies the existing formulation rather than changing its minimizer or adding mathematical reasoning.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction replace claims of outperforming previous work or the state of the art with improvement over the K-Planes baseline. Corresponding superiority claims disappear from table captions, substantially narrowing a main contribution; the pre-trained-prior novelty claim remains.

C2.justification: Table 3 newly qualifies Ha-NeRF and CR-NeRF timing results as using half-resolution training, adding relevant context for interpreting the comparison. The mechanism explanations, training-cost limitation and impact statement remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Table 6 explicitly reports fitting and refining iteration counts, and Table 3 newly discloses the two comparators' half-resolution setting. Software versions, hardware, remaining hyperparameters and the promise of future open-source code are unchanged.

R1.justification: Positioning shifts from surpassing prior state-of-the-art methods to improving the underlying representation, and Section 4.3 removes its explicit characterization of CR-NeRF as concurrent work. Section 2 and the bibliography are unchanged.

P1.justification: Targeted edits affect the abstract, contribution list, evaluation discussion and captions. The section and appendix organization remains intact; the unchanged impact statement moves from page 9 to page 8 through reflow.

P2.justification: Table 2 loses two rows and updates grouping and ranking emphasis. Table 3 adds asterisks and a footnote, while Table 6 changes row labels. All twelve figures retain identical visual content.

improvement.justification: v3 improves claim calibration and clarifies training settings, but removes Ha-NeRF and CR-NeRF quality comparisons without explaining why. CR-NeRF's reported SSIM exceeded RefinedFields on two scenes in v2, so this removes material comparative context. The PDFs do not establish whether the omission corrects unsuitable comparisons or weakens useful coverage, leaving the net quality effect uncertain.
